statement: If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact there be drawn across, in the circle, a straight line cutting the circle, the angles which it makes with the tangent will be equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle.
heath_proof: For let a straight line EF touch the circle ABCD at the point B, and from the point B let there be drawn across, in the circle ABCD, a straight line BD cutting it; I say that the angles which BD makes with the tangent EF will be equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle, that is, that the angle FBD is equal to the angle constructed in the segment BAD, and the angle EBD is equal to the angle constructed in the segment DCB. For let BA be drawn from B at right angles to EF, let a point C be taken at random on the circumference BD, and let AD, DC, CB be joined. Then, since a straight line EF touches the circle ABCD at B, and BA has been drawn from the point of contact at right angles to the tangent, the centre of the circle ABCD is on BA. [III. 19] Therefore BA is a diameter of the circle ABCD; therefore the angle ADB, being an angle in a semicircle, is right. [III. 31]  Therefore the remaining angles BAD, ABD are equal to one right angle. [I. 32] But the angle ABF is also right; therefore the angle ABF is equal to the angles BAD, ABD. Let the angle ABD be subtracted from each; therefore the angle DBF which remains is equal to the angle BAD in the alternate segment of the circle. Next, since ABCD is a quadrilateral in a circle, its opposite angles are equal to two right angles. [III. 22] But the angles DBF, DBE are also equal to two right angles; therefore the angles DBF, DBE are equal to the angles BAD, BCD, of which the angle BAD was proved equal to the angle DBF; therefore the angle DBE which remains is equal to the angle DCB in the alternate segment DCB of the circle.
ai_proof_text:
3.32
**Statement:** If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact there be drawn across, in the circle, a straight line cutting the circle, the angles which it makes with the tangent will be equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle.

**Step 1.** Let the straight line EF touch the circle at the point B, and from B let the straight line BD be drawn across in the circle, cutting it, so that its other extremity D lies on the circumference. From B draw BA at right angles to EF [1.11] and produce it [P2] until it meets the circumference again at A. Because EF touches the circle at B and BA is drawn from the point of contact at right angles to the tangent, the centre of the circle lies on BA [3.19]. Thus BA passes through the centre and is terminated at both ends by the circumference, so BA is a diameter of the circle [D1.17], and each of the two segments cut off by BA is a semicircle [D1.18].

**Step 2.** First suppose that BD does not pass through the centre, so that D is distinct from A and lies on one side of the diameter BA. Name the extremities of the tangent so that F lies on the same side of BA as D and E on the other side; then BD falls within the angle ABF, so that the angle ABF is made up of the angles ABD and DBF. Take a point C at random on the circumference BD remote from A (the arc from B to D not containing A), and join AD, DC, CB [P1]. The angles which BD makes with the tangent are DBF and DBE. The segment alternate to the angle DBF is the segment BAD, and the angle in it is the angle BAD; the segment alternate to the angle DBE is the segment DCB, and the angle in it is the angle DCB [D3.8].

**Step 3.** The angle ADB is an angle in the semicircle on the diameter BA, because D is a point on the circumference of that semicircle and DA, DB are joined from D to the extremities A, B of its base [D1.18, D3.8]. Therefore the angle ADB is right [3.31].

**Step 4.** In the triangle ABD the three angles BAD, ABD, ADB are together equal to two right angles [1.32]. Since the angle ADB is a right angle, subtracting it from the two right angles leaves the angles BAD and ABD together equal to one right angle [CN3].

**Step 5.** The angle ABF is right by the construction of Step 1. Since all right angles are equal to one another [P4], the angle ABF is equal to the angles BAD and ABD taken together.

**Step 6.** The angle ABF is made up of the angles ABD and DBF (Step 2). Subtracting the angle ABD from the angle ABF and from the sum of BAD and ABD, the remaining angle DBF is equal to the remaining angle BAD [CN3]. That is, the angle DBF which BD makes with the tangent is equal to the angle BAD in the alternate segment BAD.

**Step 7.** The points A, B, C, D all lie on the circumference, A and C being on opposite sides of BD, so ABCD is a quadrilateral in the circle. Therefore its opposite angles BAD and BCD are together equal to two right angles [3.22].

**Step 8.** The straight line BD stands on the straight line EF at B, so the adjacent angles DBF and DBE are together equal to two right angles [1.13].

**Step 9.** Hence the angles DBF and DBE taken together are equal to the angles BAD and BCD taken together, each pair being equal to two right angles [CN1].

**Step 10.** Of these, the angle DBF is equal to the angle BAD (Step 6). Subtracting these equals from the equal sums, the remaining angle DBE is equal to the remaining angle BCD [CN3]. That is, the angle DBE which BD makes with the tangent is equal to the angle DCB in the alternate segment DCB.

**Step 11.** It remains to consider the case in which BD passes through the centre. Then BD is a diameter [D1.17], and the straight line joined from the centre to the point of contact B lies along BD and is perpendicular to the tangent EF [3.18]; hence BD is perpendicular to EF, and each of the angles DBF and DBE is right [D1.10]. The two segments into which BD divides the circle are semicircles [D1.18], and the angle in each of them is right [3.31]. Since all right angles are equal to one another [P4], each of the angles DBF and DBE is equal to the angle in the segment alternate to it.

**Step 12.** Therefore, in every case, the angles which the straight line BD drawn from the point of contact makes with the tangent EF are equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle. Q.E.D.
